summary: ansible.builtin and ansible.legacy are synthetic collections: builtin covers only plugins shipped with ansible-core, while legacy (the default for short names) also includes custom plugins from configured paths that can override builtins.
questions: What's the difference between ansible.builtin.shell and shell?
Can a local module override a builtin one?

answer_card.title: ansible.builtin vs ansible.legacy
answer_card.answer_md:
- **`ansible.builtin`**: only plugins shipped with ansible-core.
- **`ansible.legacy`**: builtin **plus** custom plugins in configured/adjacent paths, which can override builtins of the same name.

A short name like `shell` means `ansible.legacy.shell`. Use `ansible.builtin.shell` to be sure you get the core module.
